page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.64-256 is a compute instance based on the 64-bit Arm architecture. The server is equipped with Ampere Altra processors running at a sustained frequency of 3.0 GHz. It features 64 physical cores mapped directly to 64 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, granting each virtual CPU a dedicated execution pipeline. The configuration includes 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

This instance does not bundle local NVMe or solid-state disk storage, requiring persistence to be managed via remote network-attached block storage volumes. Similarly, the instance contains zero discrete GPUs, focusing hardware allocation purely on general CPU and memory resources. Architectural flags indicate that x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX are not present, consistent with the Arm64 instruction set implementation.

The 1:1 ratio between physical cores and vCPUs eliminates hardware resource sharing across sibling threads, providing predictable per-core execution consistency. Qualitatively, the Ampere Altra platform delivers high core density and favorable cost efficiency for Arm-compatible multi-threaded operations. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.64-256 is well suited for containerized microservice clusters, high-concurrency web serving, CI/CD build environments, and general-purpose backend applications requiring consistent core dedication.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.64-256 is an Arm-based general-purpose instance powered by Ampere Altra processors operating at 3.0 GHz. It delivers 64 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, providing 64 vCPUs accompanied by 256 GB of system memory at a balanced 4.0 GB per core. The server does not bundle local disk storage, relying on network-attached block storage for persistent data, and features no hardware GPU accelerators. With dedicated execution pipelines per vCPU, it avoids the resource contention common to simultaneous multithreading designs. This configuration provides high thread density and solid qualitative cost efficiency for horizontally scalable workloads. It is appropriate for multi-threaded compilation tasks, CI/CD build farms, container orchestration nodes, web application serving, and Arm-native enterprise application deployments.
